title: Insured Plan of Care — Benefit Verification and Plan Activity Intervals
content:
These intervals are set per payer program of the **Insured Plan of Care**: when benefits are verified before the initial evaluation, how often they are verified again, and how long a plan may go without visits or stay on hold.

| Payer program | Verify before the initial evaluation (business days) | Re-verify at the first visit of each new calendar year | Maximum days between verifications | Hold limit before discharge (calendar days) | Days without a billed visit before an inactivity hold |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial PPO Plan of Care | 2 | Yes | 90 | 30 | 30 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Plan of Care | 2 | Yes | 90 | 30 | 30 |
| Commercial POS Plan of Care | 2 | Yes | 90 | 30 | 30 |
| Commercial HMO Plan of Care | 2 | Yes | 90 | 30 | 30 |
| Medicare Part B Plan of Care | 1 | Yes | 90 | 30 | 30 |
| Medicare Advantage Plan of Care | 2 | Yes | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Medicaid Managed Care Plan of Care | 1 | Yes | 30 | 30 | 30 |

## Questions the table answers

**By when must benefits be verified for a new evaluation?** By the stated number of business days before the initial evaluation: 2 business days on the commercial programs and Medicare Advantage, 1 business day on Medicare Part B and Medicaid Managed Care.

**Are benefits verified again at the turn of the year?** Yes on every payer program: benefits are re-verified at the first visit of each new calendar year.

**What is the longest gap allowed between verifications on an active plan?** 90 calendar days on the commercial programs and Medicare Part B; 30 calendar days on Medicare Advantage and Medicaid Managed Care.

**How long may a plan stay on hold?** 30 calendar days on every program before it is discharged for non-attendance.

**When does a quiet plan go on hold?** After 30 calendar days without any billed visit, on every program, an active plan is placed on hold for inactivity.
